title: Gate spend and brief the decision
learning_outcome: Set a cost ceiling and prepare a human decision with evidence and options.
exercise: Build a mock spend envelope and a decision brief that can end in hold.

The workbook adds currency, requesting role, forbidden actions, and revocation. In the Harbor case, use a proposed forty-dollar print test with the course printer and a two-day window. scenes.narration_exact: “Harbor's preparation role has no payment authority. It may draft a spend request; it cannot place an order, enter a card, increase a cap, or trigger paid API usage. Put a closed gate between the proposed envelope and any dollar-moving verb. If the cost, vendor, window, or evidence changes, the paper envelope goes back to Morgan. If it expires, it stays closed. A prior approval of the session idea would not approve the print order. The approval has to match the action.”

scenes.narration_exact: “Now write the decision Morgan actually owns. Chapter Eighteen uses five sections: context, options, recommendation, reversibility, and what would change our mind. Option A is to propose a session subject to facilitator confirmation. Option B is to hold the proposal and gather a fresh staffing commitment. Give B a fair case: it protects Harbor from promising a session it cannot staff. The recommendation can favor A only if the brief clearly carries that condition. Morgan can also choose hold. The agent's framing must leave room for disagreement.”

scenes.narration_exact: “Put the spend question on its own line. Even if Morgan favors a conditional session proposal, the print request remains held. The brief should name Morgan as decision owner, the course deadline, the evidence gap, and what can be reversed. A draft brief can be withdrawn. A flyer sent into the community cannot be pulled back with the same ease. That difference is why preparation and side effects have different gates. An honest decision brief makes the strongest alternative visible and tells the reviewer what evidence would overturn the recommendation.”

scenes.narration_exact: “Fill a Spend Envelope, then a Decision Brief. Give the envelope an exact illustrative amount, named course counterparty, purpose, window, one-or-zero retry limit, trace, human approver, and revocation condition. Mark it unapproved. Give the brief two real options, a fair case for the rejected option, a recommendation, reversibility, evidence gap, and a hold outcome. Keep the facilitator unconfirmed. Use a fictional or approved example. Do not use private operational data, open a checkout, use a card, call a provider, or publish a session.”
scenes.on_screen_copy_exact: Exercise card below; 3:20 quiet writing timer with optional pause.
scenes.exercise_prompt_exact: Draft a `Spend Envelope` for a fictional proposed expense and a `Decision Brief` for the Harbor session choice. The envelope must identify exact amount and currency, counterparty, purpose, execution window, retry limit, source trace, requesting role, approving human, expiry/revocation, and forbidden actions. The brief must offer at least two fairly argued options, the case against its recommendation, reversibility, what would change the recommendation, owner, deadline, and an explicit `hold` disposition. Neither document grants authority.
